questions.q: What does data virtualization do differently from every data-synchronization pattern covered earlier in this chapter?
options: It copies data into Salesforce on a faster schedule than batch sync
It requires every external record to be duplicated nightly
It only works with Platform Events, never with REST or OData
It accesses remote data live, at query time, without ever copying it into the local system
questions.explain: Data virtualization's defining trait is that no copy is ever made — each query reaches back to the real source system live, rather than querying a locally stored replica as every sync pattern in this chapter does.

questions.q: Why do external objects in Salesforce Connect generally not support formula fields, validation rules, or workflow automation built directly on them?
options: Because external objects are deprecated and being phased out
Because those features depend on data actually being stored in Salesforce's own database, and an external object's data is never stored there
Because external objects can only be created by Salesforce support, not by admins
Because formula fields only work with the Cross-Org adapter
questions.explain: External objects don't store their data in Salesforce at all — every query reaches the external system live — so features like formula fields, validation rules, and workflow that depend on locally stored data generally aren't available on them.

questions.q: What does the Cross-Org adapter connect to, and how?
options: A legacy mainframe, using a custom Apex-built protocol
Any OData 2.0 or 4.0 compliant system
Data in a different Salesforce org, using that org's own Lightning Platform REST API under the hood
Only Salesforce Marketing Cloud, via a dedicated connector
questions.explain: The Cross-Org adapter is specifically built for multi-org architectures, connecting to a different Salesforce org's data via that org's own Lightning Platform REST API, without replicating the data.

questions.q: What is the central cost of data virtualization compared to data replication, per this lesson?
options: Every query against virtualized data depends on the external system being available and fast enough to answer in real time, with no local copy to fall back on if it's down or slow
Virtualized data is always less accurate than replicated data
Virtualization always costs more in Salesforce storage than replication
Virtualization cannot be combined with replication in the same org
questions.explain: Virtualization trades storage savings and always-current data for a real-time dependency: if the external system is slow or unavailable, the external object becomes effectively unusable at that moment, since there's no local fallback copy.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is the choice between virtualization and replication always all-or-nothing for a given dataset?
options: Yes, a dataset must be either fully virtualized or fully replicated with no middle ground
No, but mixing the two approaches is considered an anti-pattern and should always be avoided
Yes, Salesforce Connect technically prevents mixing virtualized and replicated data in the same org
No — many real architectures replicate frequently-accessed or automation-critical fields while leaving less-critical, rarely-needed data virtualized through Salesforce Connect
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes that the choice isn't binary in practice: architects commonly replicate the subset of data that's frequently accessed or needed for automation/reporting, while leaving the rest virtualized through Salesforce Connect.
